headline: FIREFLY DRILLS 42m AT 6.1% CUEQ IN NEWFOUNDLAND — 9.8m AT 16.5% IN HIGH-GRADE CORE; PEA DUE JULY-AUG (TSX:FFM)
snippet: FireFly Metals (ASX:FFM, TSX:FFM) released July 2 drill results from its Green Bay project in Newfoundland showing 42.0 metres at 6.1% copper equivalent (including 9.8m at 16.5% CuEq) in hole MUG26-053 and 51.5 metres at 4.9% CuEq (including 17.0m at 9.1% CuEq) in MUG26-054, demonstrating broad high-grade mineralisation at the convergent core where upper VMS lenses meet the footwall stringer copper zone. A mid-year resource update feeds directly into a preliminary economic assessment and scoping study expected July–August 2026; the company holds A$219.9 million in cash and investments.

headline: GOLD CLAWS BACK ABOVE $4,000 AFTER WORST QUARTERLY LOSS SINCE Q4 2024 — GOLDMAN HOLDS $4,900 YEAR-END TARGET
snippet: Gold rose to $4,068 on July 2, 2026, up 0.92% on the day, beginning a recovery after gold closed June at $4,014 — capping a 14% quarterly decline from its January 28 all-time high of $5,589, the first quarterly loss since Q4 2024. Goldman Sachs reaffirmed its year-end target of $4,900/oz, arguing that central bank accumulation (averaging 1,000 tonnes annually for four consecutive years) and seasonal tailwinds shifting positive from mid-July underpin the structural bull thesis; J.P. Morgan projects $6,000/oz by Q4 2026.

headline: US COPPER TARIFF REPORT DELIVERED JUNE 30 — COMEX HITS RECORD 652,000 TONNES; GOLDMAN SEES $14,000/t IF DUTY LANDS
snippet: The U.S. Commerce Department delivered its Section 232 copper market report to the President on June 30, 2026, triggering a potential tariff decision on refined copper imports; U.S. buyers front-ran the deadline, pushing COMEX copper inventories to a record 652,200 tonnes while LME stocks fell to a near three-month low of 352,100 tonnes. Goldman Sachs forecasts copper could surge above $14,000 per tonne if refined copper tariffs take effect, amplifying a 600,000-tonne 2026 market deficit already forecast by Morgan Stanley — the largest refined deficit in more than 20 years.

headline: SILVER HOLDS BELOW $60 AS STRUCTURAL DEFICIT ENTERS SIXTH YEAR — CHINA ABSORBED 790+ TONNES IN EARLY 2026
snippet: Silver spot was trading at $58.74 per ounce on July 1, 2026, up 0.96% on the day but far below its January high of around $80/oz and unable to reclaim the $60 threshold that marked the peak of the 2025–26 bull run. The structural demand picture remains intact — China imported more than 790 tonnes of silver in early 2026 driven by solar panel and EV production — and analysts at Metals Focus see the global physical deficit extending into a sixth consecutive year as industrial offtake outstrips flat mine supply.

headline: LI-FT POWER GROWS YELLOWKNIFE LITHIUM BIG EAST AT DEPTH — 50.4Mt AT 1.00% Li2O, 1.32% Li2O OVER 17m (TSXV:LIFT)
snippet: Li-FT Power Ltd. (TSXV:LIFT) released June 30 results from 20 holes (5,324m) of its winter and summer programs at the Yellowknife Lithium Project in the Northwest Territories, confirming extensions at the BIG East complex at depth: hole YLP-0320 intersected 1.32% Li2O over 17m and YLP-0321 cut through a 100m corridor hosting eight pegmatite dykes. The company's consolidated inferred mineral resource sits at 50.4 million tonnes at 1.00% Li2O (506,000t Li2O contained), positioning Yellowknife as one of the largest spodumene projects in North America; the BIG East system remains open to the south and at depth.

headline: KALO GOLD CONFIRMS 1.8km EPITHERMAL GOLD SYSTEM IN FIJI — STEP-OUTS FIND NEW CENTRES, CSAMT GEOPHYSICS LAUNCHING (TSXV:KALO)
source_name: Investing News Network / Kalo Gold Corp. (TSXV:KALO)
snippet: Kalo Gold Corp. (TSXV:KALO) announced June 30 that two wide-spaced reconnaissance drill holes at Wainikoro on its Vatu Aurum Project in Fiji — separated by 1,027 metres — confirmed fault-controlled gold-bearing epithermal quartz veins in both holes, with mineralisation in VA26-DH18 extending beyond the main 1.8-kilometre magnetic-low target and indicating multiple potential mineralised centres. Fender Geophysics has been contracted to run CSAMT, IP, and gravity surveys over Wainikoro commencing mid-July 2026 to refine drill targets ahead of the next phase.

headline: BLOSSOM GOLD DRILLS 81.5m AT 0.385 g/t AU IN NEVADA HEAP-LEACH TARGET — 3 RIGS TURNING, 24,000m PROGRAM (TSX:BGAU)
snippet: Blossom Gold Inc. (TSX:BGAU) reported June 30 initial results from its 2026 exploration program at the Rosebud open-pit, heap-leach project in Pershing County, Nevada — a 24,000-metre campaign running three drill rigs. Standout intervals included BG26-007 returning 81.5 metres at 0.385 g/t gold from 27.1m and BG26-005 with 18.3 metres at 0.794 g/t gold from 126.5m, with the deposit oxidised to approximately 100 metres and free of refractory mineralisation. Approximately 9,337 metres of the 24,000-metre program have been completed, with resource expansion the primary objective.

headline: URANIUM LONG-TERM PRICE HITS $93/lb — HIGHEST SINCE 2008 AS AI DATACENTERS STACK ON TOP OF NUCLEAR RENAISSANCE
snippet: The uranium long-term price indicator rose to US$93.00 per pound as of March 31, 2026 — the highest level in more than 18 years, marking a US$6.50 increase since December 2025 — while the spot price held at $85.50/lb on June 30, still 9.55% above year-ago levels after consolidating from a January high above $101/lb. A new demand layer is forming as Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta signed agreements for fresh nuclear capacity to power AI data centers, adding technology-sector demand on top of the existing structural supply deficit created by Russian sanctions, Western mine underinvestment, and surging reactor build rates.

headline: HAMILTON: GOLD LEAST-OVERBOUGHT IN YEARS ENTERING SUMMER DOLDRUMS — 25-YEAR DATA SETS UP STRONG AUTUMN RALLY
snippet: In his July 2026 seasonal analysis, Adam Hamilton of Zeal LLC notes that gold has entered its weakest seasonal window — compressed into June and early July — but the technical setup is unusually bullish: January's speculative froth has been fully beaten out and gold is at its least-overbought readings in several years. Reviewing 25 years of bull-market data, Hamilton argues the reduced odds of a significant July selloff materially raise the probability of a strong autumn rally beginning as early as mid-July, making the current correction an accumulation window for both metal and mining equity investors.

headline: ZIJIN'S C$5.5B ALLIED GOLD GRAB ON TRACK — JULY 29 CLOSE AFTER COMESA, ECOWAS, INVESTMENT CANADA GREEN LIGHTS
snippet: Allied Gold Corporation (TSX:AAUC) confirmed receipt of the final outstanding regulatory approvals — from COMESA, ECOWAS, and under Canada's Investment Canada Act — for Zijin Gold International's C$5.5 billion ($44/share cash) takeover, setting a July 29, 2026 Outside Date for closing. The acquisition, the largest in Zijin Mining's history, will add three large-scale open-pit gold mines across Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, and Ethiopia (including the Kurmuk mine scheduled for commissioning in H2 2026), positioning Zijin to hit its 100-tonne gold production target ahead of schedule.

headline: CHINA LOCKS DOWN RARE EARTH LICENSING — WESTERN BUYER APPROVAL RATES COLLAPSE AS EXPORT CONTROLS REDRAW SUPPLY CHAINS
snippet: China, which controls roughly 90% of global rare earth processing and 80% of tungsten refining, has introduced strict new enforcement rules for its 2026 rare earth export licensing regime — with approval rates for European industrial firms falling below 25% in key sectors, triggering price spikes of up to sixfold outside China. Updated January 2026 controls expanded restrictions to cover rare-earth compounds including samarium, gadolinium, and lutetium critical for defence and clean-energy magnets. The U.S. government responded with a $10 billion Export-Import Bank–backed strategic mineral reserve (Project Vault) and a $1.6 billion equity stake in USA Rare Earth (USAR), but analysts say self-sufficiency remains years away.
